title: She looked powerful.
paragraphs: She looked powerful.
That’s why no one questioned her.
And that’s exactly how control hides.

You’ve seen it.
Maybe… you’ve felt it.

Confidence that feels heavy.
Influence that quietly suffocates.
Words that sound strong—but leave your spirit shrinking.
And here’s the uncomfortable truth the image whispers louder than words:
Not all strength is submitted to God.
Some of it is rebellion wearing a crown.

Jezebel didn’t scream weakness.
She radiated control.
Scripture says in 1 Kings 21:25, there was no one like Ahab who sold himself to do evil “urged on by Jezebel his wife.”
Read that slowly.

She didn’t just exist beside evil.
She fueled it.
That’s the danger.

Control doesn’t always oppose God loudly.
Sometimes it guides others away from Him quietly.
And here’s where it gets personal.

Because this isn’t just about a queen from ancient Israel.
This is about the subtle places in us where control replaces trust.
Where we:

— manipulate outcomes instead of praying
— pressure people instead of loving them
— protect our image instead of surrendering our hearts
— stay silent when God says speak… and speak when God says wait
Let me ask you something that might sting a little:
Are you trusting God… or managing everything so you don’t have to?
Because those are not the same.

Jezebel’s spirit wasn’t just dominance.
It was deep unbelief disguised as confidence.
She needed control because she didn’t trust God’s authority.
And if we’re honest…
So do we sometimes.

We call it leadership.
We call it wisdom.
We call it “just being strong.”
But heaven sees the root.

And Proverbs 3:5–6 cuts through the illusion:
“Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding…”

Not some of your heart.
Not when it’s convenient.
All.
Here’s the AHA moment:
Control is what we use when we’re afraid God won’t come through.
Let that sit.

Because suddenly, it’s not about personality anymore.
It’s about faith.
And here’s the mirror you can’t ignore:
If I need to control everything, I don’t fully trust the One who holds everything.
This is where many believers quietly drift.

We worship God publicly…
but privately we’re still trying to be Him.
That’s the tension.
That’s the hidden battle nobody posts about.

Spiritual on the outside.
Anxious on the inside.
Surrendered in words.
Controlling in decisions.
And here’s the piercing truth:
You cannot be filled with the Spirit while being driven by control.
Because 2 Corinthians 3:17 says, “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”

Control suffocates.
The Spirit frees.
So which one is leading you?
Now hear this—because this is where grace breaks in:

Jesus didn’t come to shame you for your control.
He came to free you from the fear behind it.
Because control is rarely about power.
It’s about fear.

Fear of being hurt again.
Fear of being overlooked.
Fear of things falling apart.
Fear that if you don’t hold it together… everything will collapse.
So you grip tighter.
You manage harder.
You push more.
But Jesus invites something radically different.

In Matthew 11:28–30, He says,
“Come to Me… all who are weary and burdened… and I will give you rest.”
Not control.
Rest.
Because at the cross, Jesus did what control never could:

He secured your future.
He carried your burden.
He absorbed your sin.
Including the sin of control.
Yes—even that.

The manipulation.
The hidden pride.
The quiet need to dominate outcomes.
Covered.
Paid for.
But not excused.
Called to be surrendered.
This is the Gospel:
You don’t have to be your own savior anymore.
Jesus already is.
So repentance looks like this:

Not just saying sorry…
but loosening your grip.

Letting God lead.
Even when it feels risky.
Even when it feels slow.
Even when it feels like you’re losing control.
Because you’re not losing.
You’re finally trusting.
And here’s who you are now:

You are not called to control your life—you are called to surrender it.
You are not the author of your story—Jesus is.
That changes everything.
So today—right now—ask yourself:
Where am I forcing what God is asking me to trust Him with?
Bring that into the light.
Name it.
Release it.
Because freedom doesn’t come when everything is in your hands.
It comes when everything is in His.

If this hit deeper than expected…
that’s not guilt.
That’s God inviting you higher.
Stay close.
Follow if you’re ready to grow.
Because the next message might uncover what you didn’t even know was still holding you.
